sanity_expectations: F_net = 0 identically for F_app <= mu_s*N (stick regime)
F_net is continuous at F_app = mu_s*N and equals 0 there (the exponential is 1 and the (1+alpha_v*...) factor is 1, so F_net = mu_s*N - mu_s*N = 0)
Just above the threshold, F_net grows from 0 and, because mu_s > mu_k, the effective friction drops rapidly via the Stribeck exp term, giving a locally super-linear rise in F_net
For large F_app the exp term vanishes and F_net ~ F_app - mu_k*N - alpha_v*(F_app - mu_s*N), so dF_net/dF_app tends to 1 - alpha_v = 0.8 (positive, slope reduced by viscous strengthening)
F_net is monotone non-decreasing in F_app over [0, 20] for these parameter values
F_net remains finite and real over the entire sampling range
excitation_report: Full expression RMS = 7.31 N (73*sigma). New term (velocity-strengthening factor 1 + alpha_v*(F_app - mu_s*N)/(mu_k*N)) reaches max |Delta| = 3.20 N (32*sigma) at F_app ~ 20 N, i.e. deep in the sliding regime where (F_app - mu_s*N)/(mu_k*N) is largest. Below the static threshold (F_app <= 4 N) F_net = 0 and the new term contributes nothing, as expected physically.
role_corrections: F_net: O->O (confirmed dependent variable, solved for explicitly)
F_app: V->V (confirmed sampling axis: the applied push is what is swept)
mu_s: V->P (overridden: static friction coefficient is a fixed material/surface property, not a sampling axis)
mu_k: V->P (overridden: kinetic friction coefficient is a fixed material property, not a sampling axis)
N: V->P (overridden: normal force is fixed for a given block/weight, not a sampling axis)
v_ref: P->P (confirmed Stribeck transition scale, fixed parameter)
alpha_v: P->P (confirmed viscous-strengthening slope, fixed parameter)
rationale: The expression is a closed-form piecewise map F_net(F_app; mu_s, mu_k, N, v_ref, alpha_v) with no derivatives or integrals, so this is an explicit relation evaluated pointwise. Physically only F_app changes as the operator ramps up the push; mu_s, mu_k, N, v_ref, alpha_v are fixed properties of the block/surface/kinematics model. Chose N = 10 N (roughly a 1 kg block), mu_s = 0.4, mu_k = 0.3 (typical dry-contact values with mu_s > mu_k), v_ref = 1 (dimensionless transition scale of order 1 so the Stribeck exponential decays over the physically relevant range of the normalized excess force), alpha_v = 0.2 (middle of the suggested 0-0.5 range so the linear viscous strengthening is clearly visible without dominating). F_app is swept from 0 to 20 N, straddling the static threshold mu_s*N = 4 N so both the flat zero regime and the fully sliding regime with visible Stribeck decay and linear velocity strengthening are sampled. Noise sigma = 0.1 N is small vs the dominant term (~7 N RMS) and the new alpha_v term still reaches ~32*sigma, so all terms — especially the new velocity-strengthening factor — are well above noise.
